chunks: Al-Abbas and Ali ibn al-Sindi together from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: Ali (peace be upon him) said regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And they mention the name of Allah on known days,' he said: 'The days of the Ten [of Dhu al-Hijjah].' And regarding His saying: 'And remember Allah during numbered days,' he said: 'The days of Tashriq.'

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: The Days of Tashriq (11th-13th Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.أَيَّامُ الْعَشْرِ: The Ten Days of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What are the 'known days' and 'numbered days' mentioned in the Quran for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides the definitive Shia exegetical link between the Quranic terms 'known days' and 'numbered days' and the specific ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah and the subsequent days of Tashriq. It underscores the ritual significance of these periods for dhikr and sacrifice, serving as the primary scriptural basis for the legal rulings on Hajj obligations and expiations found in works like Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
